newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tajik hostage-for-rebel swap underway, Tass says.
newsitem.headline: Tajik hostage-for-rebel swap underway, Tass says.

text.p: The leader of a rebel Islamic group holding 14 hostages in Tajikistan said on Friday he had started fulfilling an agreement to free the captives in exchange for other rebels, Itar-Tass news agency reported.
The Russian agency said rebel leader Bakhram Sadirov had told Russian Deputy Prime Minister Vitaly Ignatenko by telephone at 1430 GMT that the hostage-for-rebel swap was underway.
The report could not immediately be confirmed. Tajik officials expected the exchange to go ahead soon but could not confirm it was already under way.
Tass said two women hostages -- reporters from Tass and Interfax news agency -- were already heading out of the rebel camp with a driver for Russia's NTV television network.
In a complicated procedure, they would meet a group of other rebels flown in by Tajik authorities and return with them to the camp. All 14 hostages would then be freed, Tass said.

The rebels' main condition for releasing the hostages, seized more than a week ago, has been for the Tajik authorities to fly in rebel comrades from neighbouring Afghanistan and allow the two groups to meet up.
The hostages include three U.N. observers -- two from Switzerland and one from Ukraine -- four Russian journalists and four workers with the U.N. refugee agency.
Ignatenko said after an earlier conversation with Sadirov that reports that one hostage, a United Nations military observer, had been killed were not true.

The reporters have been sending frequent reports to their employers in Moscow on the rebels' satellite telephone, but it is not clear to what extent they are simply reporting what their captors tell them to say.

Tajikistan's security minister was seized last weekend when he tried to negotiate with the hostage-takers, who once backed the former Soviet republic's Islamic opposition but whose loyalties are now unclear.
The hostage crisis has highlighted the instability of Tajikistan, an impoverished former Soviet republic bordering Afghanistan and China.
